newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on Wall Street fears.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on Wall Street fears.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday amid expectations for a renewed decline on Wall Street, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.70 percent, or 1.45 points, to 206.39 on high all-share turnover of 105 million shekels against 114 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.95 percent to 214.90.

"The market was reacting to the decline of European stock markets and expectations of a similar decline on Wall Street. The whole market is waiting to see what the Dow will do on Wednesday," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.

"The session opened with mixed trading and a mild decline in the Maof shares. Only later did the market start falling as investors began to expect a sharp decline on Wall Street," said Uri Schur, a trader at Eyal Securities.
"The Maof options reflect expectations for a further decline on Thursday," Schur added. "Nevertheless, investors are optimistic because the market is awaiting approval of the 1997 budget."
"We saw some profit-taking today, but activity continues to be relatively strong. I do not belive that the positive trend has changed," Finn said.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the most active share, fell 2.0 percent to 785 on volume of 7.8 million shekels. On Tuesday, Communications Minister Limor Livnat announced plans to open the last remaining Bezeq telecommunications monopolies to competition by the end of 1998.

Other active shares include Koor Industries, which fell 1.25 percent to 28,008 on turnover of 5.1 million shekels, and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.0 percent to 151,820 on volume of 4.0 million shekels.
Elite Industries rose 4.0 percent to 1,555. Traders said the share rose on rumours that dairy products manufacturer Strauss was trying to raise its stake in the company.
